 Order

This is first bail application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of regular bail relating to FIR/Crime No. 46/2023 dated 24.12.2023 registered at Police Station Mahila Police Station, Narsinghpur for the offences punishable under Sections 450,
376, 376(2)(N), 294, 506 of the Indian Penal Code.

entities.text: Police Station Mahila Police Station, Narsinghpur
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 2. The counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the case.
It is contended that in the present case there is enormous delay of more than 7 months in lodging the First Information Report.
According to the case of the prosecution, first time the prosecutrix was subjected to offence of rape on 10.3.2023 and the First Information Report was lodged belatedly on 24.12.2023.
It is also contended that the age of the applicant was about 29 years and the prosecutrix was aged about 35 years at the time of incident and is also a widow.

sentences.text: It is also submitted that the past record of the applicant is unblemished.
The applicant is in custody since 24.12.2023 and trial would take considerable time to conclude, therefore, the applicant be released on bail.

3. The counsel for the State has opposed the application and submitted that there are direct allegations against the applicant and taking into consideration the statement of the prosecutrix recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C., the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail.

4. Heard the submissions advanced on behalf of the parties and perused the case diary.
5.
On perusal of case diary, it reflects that at the time of incident, the prosecutrix was about 35 years of age and the age of the applicant was about 29 years.
The First Information Report indicates commission of offence on 10.3.2023 and the report was lodged on 24.12.2023.

Therefore,
considering the overall facts and circumstances of the case, nature of allegation against the applicant, age of the prosecutrix as well as the applicant, the period of custody of the applicant and also that trial would take considerable time to conclude, this Court finds it to be a fit case to release the applicant on bail.
Therefore, without commenting on the merit of the case, the application is allowed.

6. It is directed that the applicant Sheikh Ashraf Khan shall be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned for his appearance before the said Court on all such dates as may be fixed by that Court in this regard during the pendency of trial.

7. It is further directed that the applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 437(3) of the Cr.P.C.
(MANINDER S. BHATTI) JUDGE PB Sheikh Ashraf Khan Bahna vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165579289/
